channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold struggles to find acceptance above $4,200; eases from two-week high amid USD uptick
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to capitalize on its modest Asian session uptick and trades below a fresh two-week high, levels just above the $4,200 mark, touched this Monday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar weakens despite higher oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD gains ground for the second consecutive day, trading around 1.4210 during the Asian hours on Monday. The upside of the pair could be restrained as the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) could receive support from higher oil prices.

item.title: WTI rises to near $69.00 despite OPEC+ hikes, Hormuz flows
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price extends its gains for the third successive day, trading around $69.00 per barrel during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: ECB’s Moulin: Central bank is in a “good position” after raising interest rates in June
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin said at the Rencontres Economiques conference in Aix-en-Provence on Saturday that the central bank is in a “good position” after raising interest rates in its June policy meeting, with inflation easing alongside the slump in oil pr

item.title: OPEC+ agrees on raising output targets, starting in August
item.description: The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies (OPEC+), including Russia, agreed to raise their output targets by 188,000 barrels a day starting in August.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar declines as NZIER splits on July decision
item.description: NZD/USD depreciates after two days of gains, trading around 0.5690 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair loses ground as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) weakens following the ANZ World Commodity Price Index, which fell 1.0% in June as easing Middle East tensions and lower oil prices weighed.

item.title: Iran confirms Strait of Hormuz service fees, rejects third-part intervention
item.description: Speaking at the World Peace Forum in Beijing on Saturday, Iran’s ambassador to China, Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli, said that Tehran is considering introducing new service fees for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, while promising “special" treatment for countries that supported Iran during the

item.title: British Pound flat lines around mid-1.3300s vs USD amid Iran tensions
item.description: The GBP/USD pair struggles to capitalize on last week's strong move higher and oscillates in a narrow band, around the 1.3350 area during the Asian session on Monday.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens under high import costs despite JGB yield hitting 30-year highs
item.description: USD/JPY extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around 161.70 during the Asian hours on Monday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) is caught in a high-stakes tug-of-war, buckling under surging import costs even as 10-year JGB yields hit a fresh 30-year high of 2.79%.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.8066 vs. 6.8047 previous
item.description: On Monday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.8066 compared to Friday's fix of 6.8047 and 6.7850 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro consolidates below mid-1.1400s as Hormuz risks support safe-haven USD
item.description: The EUR/USD pair kicks off the new week on a subdued note and oscillates in a narrow band below mid-1.1400s during the Asian session. Spot prices, however, remain within striking distance of a nearly two-week high, touched last Thursday, amid mixed fundamental cues.

item.title: Australian Dollar declines following TD-MI Inflation Gauge data
item.description: AUD/USD declines after two days of gains, trading around 0.6930 during the Asian hours on Monday. The currency pair loses ground following the release of TD-MI Inflation Gauge data, which came in at -0.4% month-over-month, against the -0.3% prior.

item.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: US Dollar's resilience faces Fed minutes and jobless claims
item.description: The upcoming week will bring a fresh test for major currency pairs as investors return from the US Independence Day holiday and continue to digest weaker US labor market data.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range trade bias stays neutral against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang notes that USD/CNH has seen a slight pickup in downward momentum, but still expects the pair to remain range-bound. The bank now looks for a lower intraday band around 6.7820–6.7940, while its 1–3 week view stays neutral, with USD/CNH likely to trade between 6.7750 and 6.8080.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Rebounds above 0.5700, bears guard 0.5750
item.description: The Kiwi Dollar clears the 0.5700 figure on Friday, clings to gains of over 0.22% against the Greenback after hitting a daily low of 0.5689. At the time of writing, the NZD/USD trades at 0.5709.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Seen consolidating in range against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank highlights that strong Singapore manufacturing and electronics PMIs underpin a constructive growth outlook, with Q2 GDP expected to exceed Q1’s 6% expansion. Against this backdrop, USD/SGD has eased slightly but remains near this year’s highs.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Bulls extend gains on PMI resilience – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes that stronger-than-expected China PMI data suggest slow but steady growth, reducing urgency for the PBoC to ease policy. The bank highlights that USD/CNY has fallen back below its 50-day moving average as Yuan strength reflects robust exports supported by the global AI boom.

item.title: Japanese Yen holds steady amid US Independence Day holiday
item.description: The USD/JPY pair posts modest gains on Friday amid thin trading due to the US Independence Day holiday. The US Dollar (USD) stabilizes against the Japanese Yen (JPY) after a sharp decline on Thursday following softer-than-expected United States (US) labor market data.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG reclaims $60 as RSI recovery targets $65 breakout
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) prices reclaim the $60.00 mark for the second straight day on Friday, extending their weekly gains to over 5.50% and trading at $62.42 amid broader US Dollar weakness, pushing the white metal to an eight-day high of $62.89.

item.title: Gold price climbs as weak NFP cool Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price rises by more than 1% on Friday as investors digest a softer-than-expected US jobs report, trimming hawkish bets despite higher inflation. At the time of writing, the XAU/USD pair trades at $4,174, after bouncing off daily lows of $4,121.

item.title: Euro: Slightly reduced upside as policy paths diverge – ABN AMRO
item.description: ABN AMRO’s Bill Diviney expects the US Dollar to weaken broadly but notes slightly less upside for EUR/USD after revising the bank’s ECB outlook and incorporating French and US election risks.

item.title: Swiss Franc eyes first weekly gain in five weeks as weak NFP delays Fed hikes
item.description: USD/CHF heads for its first weekly loss in five weeks as weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data released on Thursday weighed on the US Dollar (USD). The pair rebounds on Friday as the Greenback stabilizes, with traders reassessing the Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate outlook.

item.title: Copper: Tariff risks and Chile supply strain – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analyst Norman Liebke reports that the Copper market is focused on a potential 15% US import tariff on refined Copper, which could temporarily boost US demand and prices if implemented in 2027.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range bias with key levels against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang notes that USD/SGD’s sharp drop toward 1.2900 looks overdone, but the pair may still test support near 1.2890 in the near term before stabilising.

item.title: British Pound holds weekly gains as Fed hike doubts deepen
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) steadies against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, but it is poised to end the week with gains of over 1% as investors turn skeptical that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise interest rates at its September meeting.

item.title: WTI Crude Oil advances on softer US jobs data and lingering Middle East tensions
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trades around $68.65 at the time of writing on Friday, up 0.30% on the day, recovering part of its recent losses as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following softer-than-expected US employment data.

item.title: Euro struggles to extend gains as traders reassess Fed and ECB outlook
item.description: EUR/USD holds onto modest gains on Friday but struggles to extend its advance as the US Dollar (USD) stabilizes following Thursday's weaker-than-expected US jobs report. Market activity remains subdued as US financial markets are closed for the Independence Day holiday.

item.title: India: Credit-risk capital overhaul reshapes ratings – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale economist Kunal Kundu explains that the Reserve Bank of India’s revised Standardised Approach for credit-risk capital will tie regulatory risk weights to both borrower ratings and each agency’s historical default performance from April 2027.

item.title: Australian Dollar rises after upbeat PMIs improve sentiment
item.description: The AUD/USD pair climbs near the 0.6940 level on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) remains under pressure following softer-than-expected United States (US) labor market data released on Thursday.

item.title: Canada: Trade risks and persistence – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economists Claire Fan and Nathan Janzen assess the implications of the U.S. decision not to extend CUSMA (Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement) on July 1st.
